businessModel: Free, preinstalled on Galaxy devices; supports Samsung ecosystem, search/shopping partnerships and Galaxy AI features
updateCadence: Android: stable updates roughly monthly via Galaxy Store/Play; Windows builds roughly monthly
summary: Samsung's Chromium-based browser, default on Galaxy phones and now also on Windows: Secret Mode, Samsung Pass, Smart Anti-Tracking, cross-device continuity and AI helpers (Perplexity-powered on Windows, Ask Anything on Galaxy).
bestFor: Android users who want add-ons (ad blockers) without Chrome
People who want phone-to-PC continuity in the Samsung ecosystem
notFor: Users on iOS, macOS or Linux (not available)
Power users wanting Chrome Web Store/full extension choice
Those wanting an open-source or fully transparent browser

pros.title: Great on Galaxy
pros.detail: Deep integration with One UI, Samsung Pass, DeX and Galaxy AI.

pros.title: Add-on support
pros.detail: Android version offers Samsung's own add-on catalog including content blockers.

pros.title: Privacy tools
pros.detail: Smart Anti-Tracking and a biometric-locked Secret Mode.

pros.title: Windows version
pros.detail: Stable Windows build since March 2026 with Samsung phone sync.

pros.title: Useful AI
pros.detail: Ask Anything / assistant for page questions and summaries; Windows assistant built with Perplexity.

cons.title: Platform-limited
cons.detail: Android and Windows only; Windows AI features reported only for Korea and the US.

cons.title: Small extension store
cons.detail: Own add-on catalog only, no Chrome Web Store.

cons.title: Chromium lag unclear
cons.detail: Samsung's Chromium base version was not published in release notes found.

cons.title: Samsung account focus
cons.detail: Sync and best features depend on Samsung account and Galaxy devices.

faq.q: Is Samsung Internet now called Samsung Browser?
faq.a: Yes. Samsung renamed it to Samsung Browser in March 2026, first on Galaxy devices and then with the Windows stable release.
Yes. A stable Windows build (30.0.0.95) launched around March 25-26, 2026 for Windows 10 1809+ and Windows 11 after about five months of beta.
Android offers Samsung's own add-on store (not Chrome Web Store). Windows extension support was not verified.
